summary: @servicetitan/anvil-fonts preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a font-asset library under the @servicetitan scope, but its package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs uses hex-obfuscated identifiers (`_0x...`) to select a platform/arch-specific Bun release, download the Bun zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extract and chmod the binary, then execFileSync it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a single-line ~727 KB `@bun @bun-cjs` script with an obfuscator.io-style string array plus rotator function (WV8StW) and opaque identifiers — its behavior cannot be read from the source. The fetched Bun binary is used solely to execute this bundled opaque payload at install time; the payload has no relationship to the CSS/less/scss font assets the README documents. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: installing the package causes attacker-authored obfuscated code to execute under a freshly downloaded runtime that Node-ecosystem tooling does not inspect. The cover-story mismatch (fonts package shipping an obfuscated Bun dropper) together with obfuscated dropper identifiers is consistent with a hijacked or impersonated publish under the @servicetitan scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
